speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help you, tell me if you have noticed these symptoms are worse when you are feeding, crying, or lying flat on your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

The symptoms of stridor and wheezing worsening with feeding and neck flexion, along with post-feeding vomiting, strongly support this diagnosis. I will proceed with a detailed physical exam and imaging if further confirmation is needed, but the clinical picture is classic for this condition.
